description: RISE, the Reclamation Information Sharing Environment, is the open data system of the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation, which operates dams, reservoirs, canals and hydropower plants across the western United States. It gathers geospatial, time series and other data from water operations, hydropower, biology, water quality and infrastructure assets into one catalogue, with a map for browsing locations and geospatial services, a time series query tool to plot and download series by location, parameter and period as CSV, and an API for automated exchange. RISE replaced the Reclamation Water Information System in 2020 and meets the agency's duties under the OPEN Government Data Act; access is free without registration, though no specific licence is named on the pages read. Release 2.15.8 on 16 September 2026 added a response format parameter to all API endpoints and linked reservoir conditions to the Western Water Data Dashboard. Caveats: content differs by region and catalogue item, the API now rejects unfiltered results requests, and large CSV downloads needed recent fixes. Simulation uses: reservoir storage, inflow and release series for water supply, irrigation and hydropower operations models, drought planning in the Colorado and other western basins, and asset data for dam and canal resilience studies. Related records: the USACE National Inventory of Dams (data-usace-national-inventory-of-dams) and the USGS Water Data APIs (data-usgs-water-data-apis).
